# Tasks: Scaffold Toolchain Modernisation

**Input**: Design documents from `.github/spec/003-scaffold-toolchain-modernisation/`

**Prerequisites**: [plan.md](./plan.md), [spec.md](./spec.md), [research.md](./research.md), [data-model.md](./data-model.md), [contracts/](./contracts/), [quickstart.md](./quickstart.md)

**Tests**: Included. The plan's Constitution Check (Principle IV) requires a test and lint gate on every change. Scaffold-side behaviour changes get a test task, written first.

**Way of working**: Generate first, fix in the test plugin, then move the changes back (spec [_Delivery Approach_](./spec.md#delivery-approach), [research.md R14](./research.md#r14-working-in-a-generated-test-plugin-first)).

- **Phases 1–3 happen in the test plugin** (`$TEST_PLUGIN`). Each task is one commit in the test plugin's own Git history, and its message names the **move-back target** given in the task.
- **Phases 4–5 happen in the scaffold**. They move each test plugin commit back into the scaffold, then prove the round trip.
- **Phases 6–7** add the CI gate and documentation.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: The user story this task belongs to (US1–US5)
- **→ Target**: Where the change goes when it is moved back into the scaffold (Phase 1–3 tasks only)

## Paths

- `$SCAFFOLD`: this repository's root.
- `$TEST_PLUGIN`: the generated test plugin, by default `$SCAFFOLD/generated-plugins/<slug>/` (ignored by the scaffold's Git), with its own `git init`.
- `$TEST_CONFIG`: the plugin config the user supplies.

---

## Phase 1: Workbench Setup

**Purpose**: Generate the test plugin from the user's config and record the starting state

- [ ] T001 Receive `$TEST_CONFIG` from the user. Keep it outside the scaffold's Git history unless the user agrees to commit it; it may contain client details. Validate it with `node scripts/generate-plugin.js --validate $TEST_CONFIG`
- [ ] T002 Generate the test plugin with the **current, unchanged** generator: `node scripts/generate-plugin.js --config $TEST_CONFIG`
- [ ] T003 In `$TEST_PLUGIN`, run `git init` and commit everything as `baseline: generated by block-plugin-scaffold @ <scaffold commit SHA>`
- [ ] T004 Baseline audit in `$TEST_PLUGIN`: run `npm install`, then every standard alias in [command-aliases.md](./contracts/command-aliases.md), `composer install` and `composer run lint`. Record each result, the config file each tool actually loads (`--print-config` or debug output) and every leaked scaffold-only file in `.github/spec/003-scaffold-toolchain-modernisation/config-audit.md`. This is the starting defect list

**Checkpoint**: The test plugin exists, has a baseline commit, and its defects are recorded.

---

## Phase 2: User Story 1 in the test plugin — make it work out of the box (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: The test plugin installs, builds, lints and passes unit and end-to-end tests with the standard toolchain.

**Independent Test**: [quickstart.md Scenario A](./quickstart.md#scenario-a--the-test-plugin-works-out-of-the-box-us1) in `$TEST_PLUGIN`

All tasks in this phase are done in `$TEST_PLUGIN`, one commit each.

- [ ] T005 [US1] Rewrite `package.json` to match [generated-package-manifest.md](./contracts/generated-package-manifest.md): the plugin's own metadata, the 10 standard aliases, the current stable majors from [research.md R3](./research.md#r3-version-ranges-current-stable-majors-not-the-source-documents-numbers) (check the registry again), `engines` (Node ≥ 22.22, npm ≥ 10), `prepare: husky` and `lint-staged`. Delete `package-lock.json` and reinstall. **→ Target**: `scripts/toolchain/standard-toolchain.json` and `generatePackageJson()`
- [ ] T006 [US1] Delete the leaked scaffold-only files listed in `config-audit.md`: the scaffold's `.github/workflows/*`, `.github/skills`, `.github/spec`, `.github/projects`, `.github/schemas`, `.github/__tests__`, `.github/tests`, `.coderabbit.yml`, `.gemini`, `.gpt`, `.qodo`, scaffold reports and similar. **→ Target**: `excludePaths` in `scripts/generate-plugin.js`
- [ ] T007 [US1] Replace the config files with one per tool, as in [research.md R4](./research.md#r4-config-file-formats): `eslint.config.cjs` (flat), `.stylelintrc.json`, `.prettierrc.js`, `.npmpackagejsonlintrc.json`, `jest.config.js`. Delete `.eslintrc.cjs`, `.eslint.config.cjs`, `.stylelint.config.cjs`, `.prettier.config.cjs`, `.jest.config.cjs` and `.npmpackagejsonlintrc.cjs`. Deal with `.postcss.config.cjs` according to the audit. **→ Target**: the scaffold's root config files (copied by the generator)
- [ ] T008 [US1] Add `playwright.config.js` extending `@wordpress/scripts/config/playwright.config.js` (`testDir: './tests/e2e'`, `baseURL` from `WP_BASE_URL`, defaulting to `http://localhost:8888`). **→ Target**: the scaffold's root `playwright.config.js`
- [ ] T009 [US1] Run `npm run lint:js`, `npm run lint:css` and `npm run format`, and fix every finding in `src/`. **→ Target**: the scaffold's `src/` templates (with template tags restored)
- [ ] T010 [P] [US1] Add a `lint:fix` script (`phpcbf`) to `composer.json`, so the `lint-staged` PHP rule works (FR-026), and fix any `composer run lint` findings. **→ Target**: `generateComposerJson()` and the scaffold's root `composer.json`
- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Add `.husky/pre-commit` running `npx lint-staged`. Check that a commit containing a lint error is blocked. **→ Target**: the scaffold's root `.husky/pre-commit` (copied by the generator)
- [ ] T012 [US1] Add starter tests (FR-024): `tests/js/example.test.js` (a unit test on one block's `save`/`edit` or one hook) and `tests/e2e/blocks.spec.js` (the editor loads and each generated block can be inserted, using `@wordpress/e2e-test-utils-playwright` fixtures). **→ Target**: a new `templates/tests/` folder that the generator copies (the scaffold's own `tests/` stays excluded)
- [ ] T013 [US1] Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the plugin. It runs `npm ci`, `lint:js`, `lint:css`, `lint:pkg`, `test:unit`, `build`, `composer run lint`, and `test:e2e` against `wp-env`, on Node 22 and 24. It must call only commands the plugin defines (FR-025). **→ Target**: a new `templates/github/workflows/ci.yml` that the generator copies
- [ ] T014 [US1] Check that the plugin's PHP enqueues block and editor scripts from each `*.asset.php`, never from a hard-coded dependency list (FR-006). Fix any hard-coded list. **→ Target**: the scaffold's `inc/` and main plugin file templates
- [ ] T015 [US1] Run [quickstart.md Scenario A](./quickstart.md#scenario-a--the-test-plugin-works-out-of-the-box-us1) in `$TEST_PLUGIN`, including `test:e2e` with `npm run env:start`. Update `config-audit.md` so every baseline defect is marked fixed, together with the commit that fixed it

**Checkpoint**: The test plugin is fully green. Its commit history (`git log baseline..HEAD`) is the list of changes to move back.

## Phase 3: User Story 4 in the test plugin — modern APIs (Priority: P3)

**Goal**: Prove the Interactivity API and DataViews build in the test plugin before anything is moved back.

All tasks in this phase are done in `$TEST_PLUGIN`.

- [ ] T016 [US4] Add a throwaway `view.js` that imports `@wordpress/interactivity`, and set `viewScriptModule` in one block's `block.json`. Run `npm run build` and confirm `view.asset.php` lists the module dependency. If a build flag is needed, commit it. **→ Target**: `standard-toolchain.json → scripts` and the scaffold's `scripts/build.js` or `webpack.config.js`. Revert the throwaway files
- [ ] T017 [P] [US4] Add a throwaway admin script that imports `@wordpress/dataviews`. Confirm it builds with no extra install and that `@wordpress/dataviews` is either bundled on purpose or external, as WordPress core expects for the chosen version. Record the outcome in `config-audit.md` and revert

**Checkpoint**: Modern API readiness is proven. Everything left to move back is committed in the test plugin.

## Phase 5: Round-trip proof (US1, FR-027)

**Goal**: Regenerating from the updated scaffold reproduces the hand-fixed test plugin.

**Independent Test**: [quickstart.md Scenario F](./quickstart.md#scenario-f--round-trip-proof-fr-027)

- [ ] T035 [US1] Write `scripts/toolchain/compare-toolchain.js <dir-a> <dir-b>`, which compares only toolchain files ([spec Key Entities](./spec.md#key-entities)) and prints a unified diff. Add `scripts/toolchain/__tests__/compare-toolchain.test.js`
- [ ] T036 [US1] Regenerate from the updated scaffold with the same `$TEST_CONFIG` into a fresh folder (`--output-dir /tmp/rt`), then run `node scripts/toolchain/compare-toolchain.js $TEST_PLUGIN /tmp/rt/<slug>`. **It must show 0 differences** (SC-009). For each difference, decide whether the test plugin or the scaffold is right, fix it, and run the comparison again
- [ ] T037 [US1] In the regenerated folder, run `npm install` and all of Scenario A. It must pass with no edits

**Checkpoint**: The move-back is complete and proven. This is pull request 1.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

```text
Phase 1 (workbench) ─▶ Phase 2 (US1 in test plugin) ─▶ Phase 3 (US4 in test plugin)
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                            Phase 4 (move back) ─▶ Phase 5 (round trip) ─▶ Phase 6 (CI gate) ─▶ Phase 7 (docs)
```

- Phase 2 tasks run in order (T005 first, since the other tasks need the new packages). T010 and T011 can run alongside T009.
- Phase 3 needs T005.
- Phase 4 needs Phases 2 and 3 to be finished, so that nothing is moved back that later changed in the test plugin. The tests (T018–T020) come before T021–T031. T026–T032 run in parallel after T023.
- Phase 5 needs all of Phase 4.
- Phase 6 needs Phase 5. The fixtures (T038) come from the proven config.
- Phase 7 can start once Phase 5 has passed.

## Delivery Mapping (pull requests)

| Pull request                                          | Branch                             | Tasks                 | Source document phase                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Toolchain proven in the test plugin and moved back | `feat/003-generated-toolchain`     | T018–T037, T049, T050 | Phase 1 _Audit & Lock_ + Phase 2 _Configuration Uniformity_ |
| 2. Generation check in CI                             | `ci/003-generation-check`          | T038–T043, T049       | Phase 3 _CI/CD Pipeline Update_                             |
| 3. Docs, instructions and governance                  | `documentation/003-toolchain-docs` | T044–T048, T049, T051 | Phase 4 _Documentation & Rollout_                           |

Phases 1–3 (T001–T017) produce no scaffold pull request. Their output is the test plugin's commit history, which is linked from pull request 1 as `config-audit.md`.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Workbench first**: generate, audit, and fix until green in the test plugin (T001–T017). Nothing in the scaffold changes yet, so this is low-risk and fully reversible.
2. **Move back in one pull request**: the version jump and config changes are already proven, so moving them back is mostly mechanical. The round trip (T036) is the acceptance gate.
3. **Then lock it in**: the CI generation check stops future changes from breaking what the round trip proved.
4. Run `/speckit-analyze` before T005, to cross-check the spec, plan and tasks.
